title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 228
paragraphs: The priests also gave me a strong proof concerning this land as follows. In the reign of King Moeris, whenever the river reached a height of at least eight cubits it watered Egypt below Memphis; and not yet nine hundred years had passed since the death of Moeris when I heard these things from the priests. Yet now, unless the river rises to sixteen cubits — or fifteen at the least — it does not go over the land. I think too that those Egyptians who live below the lake of Moeris, and especially in the region called the Delta, if that land continues to grow in height according to this proportion and to expand similarly in extent, will suffer for all time to come, from the Nile failing to flood their land, the very thing they themselves said the Hellenes would one day suffer. For hearing that all the land of the Hellenes is watered by rain and not by rivers as theirs is, they said the Hellenes would one day be disappointed of a great hope and suffer the evils of famine. This saying means that if the god shall not send them rain but allow drought to prevail for a long time, the Hellenes will be destroyed by hunger; for they have in fact no other supply of water to save them except from Zeus alone.
